values.description: Default admin endpoint prefix.
Actuator-style prefix — groups admin endpoints alongside Spring Boot Actuator.
Conventional admin prefix.
Internal-service prefix — common when the admin surface is behind a separate ingress.
Allow all origins. Use only in non-production environments.
React / Vite dev server default.
Local backend serving a frontend on the same host.
Production admin UI origin — replace with your actual domain.
Safe read-only method.
Create or action method.
Full-replace method.
Partial-update method.
Delete method.
Preflight method — required for CORS; always include.
Metadata-only variant of GET.
Bearer token header — required for KEYCLOAK and BASIC auth modes.
MIME type header — required for any request with a body.
Response content-negotiation header.
XMLHttpRequest identifier header — sent by some frontend frameworks.
Distributed-tracing correlation header.
Cache directive header.
Expose the correlation ID so the browser can read it for logging.
Expose the request ID generated by the gateway or server.
Expose the Location header returned on resource creation.
Expose the ETag header for conditional requests.
Expose the Content-Disposition header for file-download responses.
Disable preflight caching — browser re-checks on every request.
10 minutes — short preflight cache, useful during development.
1 hour — default preflight cache.
24 hours — long preflight cache for stable production configurations.
OAuth2 JWT bearer auth via a ReactiveJwtDecoder. Requires spring-setting-admin-keycloak on the classpath. Fails fast at startup if the decoder bean is absent.
HTTP Basic with a hardcoded user from spring.setting.admin.web.auth.basic.*. For local dev and QA only — never enable in production.
No authentication. A synthetic Authentication carrying spring.setting.admin.web.auth.noop.roles is injected. Intended for integration tests and laptop dev.
Default admin username.
Service-scoped admin username.
